cordillera.subtitle: Explore the mountain range
cordillera.body: Venture into the Andes Mountain Range, a place where nature shows its power and beauty in every corner. From deep valleys to majestic peaks, the range invites every adventurer to discover its wonders and care for them for future generations.

esencia.title: Our essence
esencia.subtitle: A perfect blend of tradition, nature and warmth.
esencia.p1: Cómbita is a magical place in the Eastern Mountain Range, where nature expresses itself in its full beauty. Among its mountains, El Valle Regional Park displays its biodiversity: frailejones inhabit the moors, while hummingbirds fill the air with their colorful flight. This natural richness invites exploration and adventure along its trails, also home to butterflies and native birds.
esencia.p2: Cómbita's culture is felt in every corner, reflected in its traditions and friendly people. Its cuisine offers typical delicacies such as the Boyacá arepa and the region's piquete, perfect for comfort and connecting with the essence of Boyacá.
esencia.acc1_a: Cómbita lies in the heart of the Eastern Mountain Range, surrounded by imposing mountains and dreamlike landscapes. This special place invites you to explore every corner, enjoying its biodiversity, natural trails, and the beauty of an environment that embraces the visitor.
esencia.acc2_a: Dive into adventure with our treks and excursions, designed to discover the majesty of the range and its best-kept secrets. Each route is an opportunity to connect with nature, live unforgettable moments and discover the soul of Cómbita.
esencia.acc3_a: Our team is made up of passionate, expert guides who love every corner of Cómbita. Together, we work to create authentic, memorable experiences for every visitor, inviting them to become part of this great community that breathes nature and adventure.

about.title: About Cómbita | Turismo Cómbita
about.description: Discover Cómbita, Boyacá: a town full of history, nature, culture and tradition in the heart of the Colombian Andes.
about.hero_subtitle: An Andean corner where nature and tradition meet

intro.p1: Cómbita is a municipality in the department of Boyacá, Colombia, just 10 kilometers from the city of Tunja. Nestled in the Cundiboyacense highlands at an average altitude of 2,825 meters above sea level, this land offers páramo landscapes, green valleys and breathtaking mountains.
intro.p2: With a history that dates back to pre-Columbian times and a rich Muisca heritage, Cómbita preserves ancestral traditions mixed with the warmth of its people. From the administration of the Augustinian fathers in 1586 to the brave role of Clara Tocarrucho in the 1810 independence movement, every corner of the town tells a story.
intro.p3: Today, Cómbita opens up to the world as a tourist destination, welcoming those who seek authentic experiences in touch with nature, Boyacá's rural culture and the region's traditional cuisine.

unique.subtitle: Reasons to visit Cómbita
unique.nature_d: Páramo ecosystems with frailejones, crystal-clear lagoons such as Laguna Rica, and trails that cross mountain landscapes above 3,000 meters of altitude.
unique.history_d: Muisca heritage, colonial architecture, living rural traditions and the brave history of independence that you can feel in every village.
unique.food_d: Authentic flavors of country cooking: cocido boyacense, mazamorra, corn arepas, cuchuco and traditional desserts made with recipes passed down through generations.
unique.hiking_d: Trails such as La Peña, Casa Ricaurte, Cerro Tilín and Laguna Rica offer hikes for all levels surrounded by native flora and fauna.
unique.crafts_d: Wool weavings, ceramics, fique and woodwork crafted by artisans who keep the region's ancestral techniques alive.
unique.warmth_d: The hospitality of Cómbita's people is legendary. Here every visitor is welcomed as family, with a smile and a hot tinto.

history.hero_subtitle: A town that flourishes between tradition and bravery

timeline.t1_text: In 1586, the Augustinian fathers began administering the territory of Cómbita, marking a milestone in its history and laying the foundations for its organization.
timeline.t2_text: Archbishop Agustín Alvarado y Castillo decreed the construction of the parish, a place that would become the heart of the community.
timeline.t3_text: Led by Clara Tocarrucho and other brave figures, the revolt in Cómbita contributed to independence from the Spanish government, leaving a legacy of struggle.
timeline.t4_title: A town between valleys and mountains
timeline.t4_text: Cómbita continues to showcase its historical and natural richness while adapting to modernity, preserving its unique identity.

dishes.title: Typical Dishes of the Region
dishes.subtitle: Some of the traditional dishes you can taste in Cómbita
dishes.cuchuco_desc: A thick soup of cracked corn with pork ribs, potato, peas and broad beans. The most representative soup of Cómbita, ideal for the cold paramo climate.
dishes.piquete_desc: The municipality's signature platter. A variety of grilled and fried meats served with creole potatoes, arepa, yucca and guacamole. A feast to share with family.
dishes.changua_desc: Traditional Boyacá broth with milk, poached egg, green onion and cilantro. Served with calado (toast) and farmer's cheese.
dishes.caldos_desc: Comforting broths prepared with potato, ribs, beef shank or other meats. Perfect to start the day with energy in the mountain cold.
dishes.arepas_desc: Yellow corn arepas grilled over charcoal or on a wood stove, served hot with butter and fresh farmer's cheese.
dishes.envueltos_desc: Sweet tender-corn dough wrapped in corn husks and steamed. A traditional delight of the Boyacá countryside.
dishes.cuajada_melao_desc: Fresh cow's milk curd drizzled with hot panela molasses. The contrast between the salty cheese and the sweet molasses is the most authentic flavor of Cómbita.
dishes.cuajada_moras_desc: Fresh curd served with homemade blackberry jam from the region. The wild paramo blackberries give this country dessert an intense, unique flavor.
dishes.chicha_desc: Ancestral fermented corn beverage, a direct heritage of the Muisca culture. Crafted by hand, it is an essential part of Cómbita's festivities and celebrations.
dishes.jugos_desc: Natural juices of curuba, blackberry, blueberries and strawberries grown in the fertile lands of Cómbita. Fresh paramo fruits, full of flavor and vitamins.

products.title: Regional Products
products.subtitle: A tradition that lives on
products.body: Some restaurants in Cómbita are fortunate to source directly from local gardens, offering fresh and seasonal products. This practice, although not universal, represents a beautiful tradition that connects the table with the land, preserving ancestral farming techniques and guaranteeing authentic flavors in every dish.

fiestas.title: Cómbita Patron Saint Festivities
fiestas.description: A joint tribute to the Immaculate Conception, Saint Isidore the Laborer and Saint Philip. An explosion of culture combining dance festivals, displays of Boyacá folklore, sports competitions, gastronomic exhibitions featuring the best traditional dishes, traditional horseback parades and colorful artisan fairs.

semana_santa.title: Holy Week
semana_santa.description: One of the most solemn and moving celebrations of the year. It includes traditional processions through the cobblestone streets, special masses, the moving Stations of the Cross through the town, the Holy Sepulchre procession on Good Friday, the Easter Vigil on Saturday and the joyful Resurrection mass on Sunday.
semana_santa.highlight: Living Stations of the Cross, Easter Vigil

corpus.title: Corpus Christi
corpus.description: An ancestral tradition dating back to colonial times. Locals create beautiful altars decorated with harvest produce, symbolizing gratitude for the fertility of the land and unity in faith. The procession around the main square is one of the most moving moments, with carpets of colored sawdust and flower petals.

climate.intro: Cómbita has a cold mountain climate. Months marked with ★ are the best to visit.

pack.title: What to Pack?
pack.intro: Pack smart to make the most of your experience in the Boyacá páramo.

recs.title: Important Recommendations
recs.nature_d: Don't leave litter on the trails. Frailejones take more than 100 years to grow; don't pull or touch them. Respect the wildlife.
recs.altitude_d: We are above 2,800 meters. If you come from lowlands, take it easy your first day. Drink plenty of water and avoid strenuous activity during the first hours.
recs.guide_d: For páramo hikes it is advisable to go with a certified guide. They know the routes and the weather and can make your experience much richer.
recs.weather_d: Weather in the páramo changes quickly. It can be sunny one minute and raining the next. Always carry a waterproof layer, even in the dry season.

food.title: Dishes You Must Try
food.intro: Boyacá cuisine is full of earthy flavors. Don't leave without trying these dishes.
food.mute_d: Thick soup with corn, beans, potato, peas, pork and beef. The signature dish of the region.
food.arepa_d: Sweet, with cheese and panela. Baked in a wood-fired oven, it has a unique, unmistakable flavor.
food.cocido_d: A variety of tubers, broad beans, corn and meats slowly cooked. Comforting and hearty.
food.aguapanela_d: Hot panela drink with pieces of farm cheese. Perfect for the cold of the páramo.
food.trucha_d: Fresh trout from mountain rivers, grilled or al ajillo. Delicate and delicious.
food.almojabanas_d: Cheese buns made with cassava starch. Crispy outside, soft inside. Ideal with hot chocolate.

hero.h2: All routes and transport options to reach Cómbita

routes.title: Main Routes
routes.intro: Two main options to reach Cómbita depending on your starting point.
routes.bogota_desc: The most common route. Take the exit via Autopista Norte to the road that leads to Tunja along the Bogotá-Tunja dual carriageway.
routes.bogota_step1: Leave Bogotá via Autopista Norte and take the road to Tunja (Route 55).
routes.bogota_step2: Continue along the dual carriageway through Zipaquirá, Ventaquemada and the Puente de Boyacá.
routes.bogota_step3: Before reaching Tunja, take the signposted exit toward Cómbita (north exit of the dual carriageway).
routes.bogota_step4: Follow the road for about 5 km until you reach the town center of Cómbita.
routes.tunja_desc: Cómbita is just a few minutes from the capital of Boyacá. It's the fastest and cheapest option.
routes.tunja_step1: From downtown Tunja, head north along Avenida Norte.
routes.tunja_step2: Take the road toward Paipa/Duitama and follow the signs to Cómbita.
routes.tunja_step3: In a few minutes you'll reach the town center of Cómbita.

bus.title: Public Transport
bus.intro: Bus and shared-van options to get there without your own vehicle.
bus.bog_tun_desc: From Bogotá's Bus Terminal (Salitre or Norte) there are frequent departures to Tunja with several companies.
bus.tun_com_desc: From Tunja there are shared vans and local buses leaving frequently to Cómbita. You can catch them at different points:
bus.tun_com_p1: Tunja Bus Terminal: Buses and shared vans with regular departures. Fare approx. $2,500 - $3,500.
bus.tun_com_p2: Avenida Norte: Shared vans that pass along the road and pick up passengers. Frequency every 10-15 minutes.
bus.tun_com_p3: Taxi: From downtown Tunja a taxi costs approximately $12,000 - $18,000.

location.title: Location
location.intro: Cómbita is located in the department of Boyacá, a few kilometers north of Tunja.

tips.title: Travel Tips
tips.warm_d: Average temperature is 13°C and can drop further at night. Bring a jacket and layered clothing.
tips.fuel_d: If you're driving, make sure to carry enough fuel. There are stations in Tunja.
tips.cash_d: Some rural establishments do not accept cards. Bring enough cash.
tips.sun_d: Due to the altitude, UV radiation is high even on cloudy days. Use sunscreen.

trek_laguna.title: Cómbita, Laguna Rica
trek_laguna.description: Hike to Laguna Rica in Cómbita, Boyacá. Páramo with frailejones, hummingbirds and mountain landscapes.

hero.subtitle: A unique experience surrounded by nature and beauty

trek_laguna.intro: The hike to Laguna Rica takes you through a unique landscape, surrounded by frailejones, orchids and vibrant local wildlife. This medium-level route offers stunning valley views while you enjoy the kind of tranquility only a place like this can provide. The lake, set in the heart of the El Valle Regional Park, is a natural refuge that invites reflection and a deep connection with nature. A must-visit for those seeking adventure and serenity in a single place.
trek_laguna.guide_text: Hiring a local guide is recommended for this páramo route. They know the trails, the shifting weather and the endemic flora.
trek_laguna.body: The hike to Laguna Rica is medium-level and offers stunning views of the valley. Along the way you can see frailejones, hummingbirds and orchids. The trail, surrounded by Andean flora, lets visitors enjoy the calm of the páramo and the majesty of the nearby mountains. It is a unique experience for anyone seeking to connect with nature at its fullest.

difficulty.heading: Medium difficulty
difficulty.text: A medium-difficulty route, ideal for those looking for a challenging yet accessible hike surrounded by impressive natural landscapes.

trek_pena.title: Cómbita, La Peña
trek_pena.description: Hike to La Peña in Cómbita, Boyacá. A rocky outcrop with panoramic views of the Boyacá highlands.

hero.subtitle: The most imposing and highest spot in all of Cómbita

trek_pena.intro: The hike to the La Peña Viewpoint is medium-high difficulty, ideal for those seeking a challenge and an impressive reward upon reaching the summit. This is the highest point in Cómbita and offers one of the most striking views in the whole region. From its height, visitors can take in a sweeping panorama of the mountain range and the valleys around the municipality, connecting deeply with the natural surroundings. An experience that combines effort and awe, perfect for those who love heights and unique landscapes.
trek_pena.guide_text: For this medium-high difficulty route an experienced local guide who knows the terrain and páramo conditions is recommended.
trek_pena.body: La Peña is the highest and most imposing point in all of Cómbita, located in the Santa Bárbara village within the La Peña Páramo. The route climbs from 2,825 m in town up to 3,200 m, crossing grasslands, cloud forest and finally páramo. From the top, the rocky outcrop offers a 360-degree panorama covering the cordillera, the surrounding valleys and, on clear days, the city of Tunja.

difficulty.heading: Medium-high difficulty
difficulty.text: A medium-high difficulty route, ideal for those seeking a challenge with a reward: panoramic views from the highest point in Cómbita.

trek_valle.title: Cómbita, Casa Ricaurte
trek_valle.description: Route to Casa Ricaurte in Cómbita, Boyacá. Historic and cultural tourist attraction in the rural area.
trek_valle.intro: Casa Ricaurte is a historic tourist attraction located in the rural area of Cómbita. This cultural point of interest offers a connection to the municipality's history and heritage. Surrounded by the mountainous landscape of the eastern cordillera, the route to Casa Ricaurte lets visitors enjoy panoramic views and the calm of the Boyacá countryside. The walk crosses rural paths where you can see the everyday life of the villages and the region's traditional architecture.
trek_valle.guide_text: A local guide is recommended to explore the páramo. They know the trails and can identify the endemic flora and fauna.
trek_valle.body: Casa Ricaurte is a site of historical and tourist interest in Cómbita. Located in the rural area of the municipality, this attraction offers a tour of the local history and cultural heritage of the region. The natural surroundings, framed by mountains and Andean vegetation, complement the experience with beautiful landscapes. It is an ideal stop for those who wish to explore the historic and cultural side of Cómbita.

difficulty.heading: Medium-low difficulty
difficulty.text: A medium-low difficulty route, ideal for those seeking a challenging yet accessible hike surrounded by impressive natural landscapes.

see.oak_value: One of the oldest in the Andes

trek_tilin.title: Cómbita, El Tilín
trek_tilin.description: Hike to Cerro Tilín in Cómbita, Boyacá. Pre-Columbian rock paintings and ancient rock formations.

hero.subtitle: An easy-access experience, perfect for families

trek_tilin.intro: The hike to El Tilín takes you to a site rich in ancestral Muisca history in the San Francisco village, about 5 km from downtown Cómbita. The route, low-difficulty and family-friendly, leads to a 10- to 12-meter waterfall next to rock formations with basins carved by Indigenous peoples for consecration rituals. Oral tradition says that on full-moon nights you can hear a sound like a small bell, which is where its name comes from. A must-visit for those who want to connect with archaeological heritage and nature in a single place.
trek_tilin.guide_text: For a richer experience, contact a local guide who knows every corner of the trail and its Muisca history.
trek_tilin.body: The hike to El Tilín is low-difficulty, ideal for those looking for a calm experience full of history. On this easy route, visitors can admire rock paintings telling ancestral stories while walking alongside the soft murmur of a stream. Along the way, small waterfalls dot the landscape, creating a relaxing atmosphere. The trail also passes near a Muisca burial site, an important cultural relic that offers a deep connection with the history of the native peoples. It is an accessible and enriching route for those who want to explore nature and local culture.

difficulty.heading: Low difficulty
difficulty.text: A low-difficulty route, ideal for those looking for an accessible hike surrounded by impressive natural landscapes.

see.moyas_value: Ritual hollows carved into the rock

trek_centro.title: Historic Center | Turismo Cómbita
trek_centro.description: Tour of the historic center of Cómbita, Boyacá. Colonial church, main square and traditional streets.

hero.title: Historic Center
hero.subtitle: The cultural and religious heart of Cómbita

trek_centro.intro: The tour of the historic center of Cómbita is a quiet, enriching walk that reveals the essence of the municipality. The starting point is the main square, known as the "Mano de Tigre" plaza, where the imposing Church of the Immaculate Conception stands, whose construction was ordered in 1776 by Archbishop Agustín Alvarado y Castillo. The cobblestone streets of the center keep the charm of traditional Boyacá architecture, with colorful house facades and wooden balconies that tell the town's story.

free_tour.title: Self-guided tour
free_tour.text: The historic center is open access. You can explore it at your own pace and enjoy the architecture, local food and the warmth of the people of Cómbita.

trek_centro.body: The town of Cómbita preserves the classic colonial layout of Boyacá villages. Around the main square stand the most emblematic buildings: the Church of the Immaculate Conception, the Town Hall and the traditional houses with their white facades and colorful doors. A walk through its streets is a journey to the past, where the calm and warmth of its people make visitors feel at home.

facts.distance_tunja_value: 8.5 km along the Northern Central Highway

difficulty.heading: Easy difficulty
difficulty.text: A flat, accessible route for the whole family, ideal for getting to know the history and culture of Cómbita without physical effort.

what_to_see.title: What to see
what_to_see.plaza_value: Main square with fountain and gardens

trek_sendero.title: Cómbita, Laguna Negra
trek_sendero.description: Laguna Negra in the Cómbita páramo, Boyacá. Demanding full-day trek above 3,400 m among frailejones and high-Andean forest. Guide required.
trek_sendero.intro: Laguna Negra is a páramo lake located in the highlands of Cómbita, more than 3,400 meters above sea level. Its dark, calm waters reflect the Andean sky surrounded by centuries-old frailejones and páramo vegetation. The route is demanding: a full-day trek that climbs from high-Andean forest into the heart of the páramo, crossing uneven terrain, dense fog and sharp temperature changes. Good physical condition is required and going with a local guide who knows the area is mandatory. Not suitable for young children or people with heart or respiratory problems.

box.title: High-mountain trekking
box.text: A demanding full-day walk over páramo terrain. A local guide is mandatory and good physical condition is needed.

trek_sendero.body: The climb to Laguna Negra is one of the most demanding routes in the Cómbita páramo. The path starts in high-Andean forest and climbs steep terrain past 3,400 meters, crossing boggy areas, tussock grass and extensive frailejón fields. The weather is unpredictable: intense sun, thick fog and rain can alternate within minutes. The reward is reaching the dark, serene waters of the lake, a natural mirror surrounded by absolute silence at the heart of the páramo.

difficulty.heading: High difficulty
difficulty.text: Demanding trek with a long climb over uneven páramo terrain. Good physical condition and experience with mountain hiking are required.

recommendations.clothing_value: Thermal layers, waterproof jacket and windbreaker
recommendations.footwear_value: Waterproof trekking boots or rubber boots
recommendations.bring_value: Sunscreen, energy snacks, dry change of clothes and flashlight
